question: According to Fashionphile's 2023 Ultra Luxury Resale Report, find which Hermes bag is the most popular for resale. Then, based on the upcoming 2024 price increases article from PurseBlog.com, determine if it would be cheaper to buy it in Europe or US. If there are multiple sizes listed for the same bag, pick the larger one from the list, the numbers next to the bag names are the sizes. Let's use the average 2023 exchange rate of 1 USD to 0.924 EUR.

answer:
Need most popular Hermes bag in Fashionphile report. In report section "Most Popular Bags" earlier shows list includes Hermes Evelyne TPM, but no unit numbers shown. Need which is most popular. The list shows:

- Louis Vuitton Pochette Metis
- Chanel Wallet on Chain
- Gucci Soho Disco Bag
- Hermes Evelyne TPM
- Saint Laurent Lou Camera Bag

Thus the most popular among Hermes is Evelyne TPM. So answer: Hermes Evelyne TPM.

Need decide if cheaper to buy in Europe or US. Use PurseBlog 2024 price increase article: have US 2024 price and EU price. For Evelyne TPM, US 2024 price $3,850 (actually from table: Evelyne III 29 had 3,850). Wait that's 2024 price. For EU price: look at table EU. Evelyne III 29 is in EU list: 2024 price €2,900? Wait EU table shows Evelyne III 29 – Yes price 2024 €2900. Let's confirm. In EU table: "Evelyne III 29 | Clemence | €2900". For US: It's $3,850. USD to EUR 0.924. Convert US price to EUR: $3,850 * 0.924 = 3,850 *0.924 = 3,546. (Calculate precise: 3850*0.924= 3850*0.9=3465; plus 3850*0.024=92.4; sum=3557.4). So US price ~ €3,557.

Thus cheaper to buy in Europe (€2,900 vs €3,557). So answer.

Need source citations: Fashionphile report for list. Provide quote. Also Purseblog tables. Provide conversion. We'll cite.
**1. Most popular Hermès bag according to the 2023 Ultra‑Luxury Resale Report**

The report’s “Most Popular Bags” section lists five standout items, the only Hermès entry being the **Hermès Evelyne TPM** (see Fashionphile’s report, “Most Popular Bags” section, image 49 and accompanying text).  
*Source: Fashionphile – 2023 Ultra‑Luxury Resale Report († see section “Most Popular Bags”)*  

**2. Which locale is cheaper if you want to buy that bag in 2024?**

| Market | 2024 price (base currency) | 2024 price (converted to €) |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **USA** | $3,850 (Evelyne III 29, Clemence) | €3,557 (calculated: $3,850 × 0.924) |
| **Europe** | €2,900 (Evelyne III 29, Clemence) | €2,900 |

*Source: PurseBlog – “Hermès Price Increase 2024 – It’s Here Already” (US prices table and Europe prices table)*  

Because the European price (€2,900) is lower than the converted U.S. price (€3,557), purchasing the Hermès Evelyne TPM in Europe would be cheaper.  

**Conclusion**  
The Hermès Evelyne TPM is the most popular Hermès bag in the 2023 Fashionphile report, and buying it in Europe is cheaper than buying it in the United States in 2024.

## 2023: The Era of Recommerce Growth

For FASHIONPHILE, this year has been about exciting recommerce growth, defined by [retail innovation](https://www.fashionphile.com/blogs/academy/ace-awards-retail-innovation/), discussions on authenticity, and [the principles of circular fashion](https://www.fashionphile.com/blogs/academy/the-rs-of-circular-fashion/). Beyond the confines of our workplace, the resale industry (and beyond) have become a hub of boundless creativity, technological progress, and diverse trends. We’ve watched as technological developments — from the integration of AI to the emergence of entirely new social platforms, like Threads — have become increasingly more commonplace in our day-to-day lives. On top of that, we’ve participated in countless conversations around topics like dupe culture, quiet luxury, and the emergence of unique micro-trends, like "Barbiecore," that have been influenced by Gen Z. Through 2023, the fashion landscape has evolved into a vibrant tapestry of intertwined influences and forms of expression.

Amidst this influx of fast-shifting trends and economic changes, this year has proven to be transformative for resale, with projections indicating that [the global secondhand market will reach an astounding $350 billion by 2027](https://wwd.com/sustainability/environment/resale-fashion-global-secondhand-market-350-billion-2027-thredup-report-2023-fast-fashion-1235602217/), nearly doubling in size since last year. Gone are the days when purchasing pre-owned items were merely seen as an alternative shopping channel. Instead, [resale has evolved into a way of life](https://www.fashionphile.com/blogs/academy/the-rs-of-circular-fashion/), embodying a deeper philosophy that reverberates with conscious consumption and sustainable practices.

Here at FASHIONPHILE, we see that this paradigm shift — one that transcends the limitations of singular ownership — can be attributed to the growing momentum of repurposing, reusing, and rewearing fashion items. This movement has gained immense traction on social media in 2023 alone, with trending hashtags such as #outfitrepeater and #rewearclothes being fueled by influential figures who feel strongly about fostering a more connected and sustainable fashion ecosystem. With [celebrities gracing the red carpets in archival dresses](https://www.vogue.com.au/fashion/archive-fashion-oscars-2023/image-gallery/dacccfed74a353d6b02e39442fce5294) and even [passing them down to younger generations](https://www.vogue.com/article/apple-martin-models-gwyneth-paltrows-2002-alexander-mcqueen-oscars-dress), the spirit of sustainability and fashion resale is more apparent today than ever before.

In the midst of these shifts toward a more circular landscape, FASHIONPHILE remains committed to providing an unparalleled platform for ultra-luxury resale. Our mission is, and always has been, to make ultra-luxury accessible to all and ensure authenticity remains an integral part of the experience — all while embracing and amplifying a circular lifestyle.

In 2023, our [expert thought leaders confidently spearheaded essential conversations](https://www.instagram.com/reel/CtmbcsttTh7/) that tackled a range of pressing issues that affect individual consumers as much as the greater fashion landscape at large. Authenticity took center stage, as [FASHIONPHILE initiated a comprehensive public dialogue about the perils of counterfeits,](https://www.fashionphile.com/blogs/academy/the-high-price-of-low-cost-fakes/) shedding light on the detrimental impact of purchasing fake products. Our unwavering [dedication to authenticity](https://account.fashionphile.com/authenticity/page) serves as the driving force behind FASHIONPHILE’s relentless efforts to educate and empower our customers, working to equip them with the knowledge and awareness to make informed choices and participate actively in the fight against counterfeits.

This conversation is only just scratching the surface. As you delve into this report, we invite you to explore the broader happenings within the resale industry from our point of view and uncover the developments that continue to shape the ultra-luxury sector. From market insights on ultra-luxury investments to emerging trends, join us as we delve deeper into the dynamic world of ultra-luxury resale for the year 2023 and beyond.

## Scarcity & Price Increases: Demand for Chanel

What do Gen Z, Millennials, and Gen X have in common? Searches for Chanel. Keeping up with Chanel’s price increases is practically a sport. We know that when [luxury brands double down on bag quotas](https://fashionista.com/2023/06/luxury-brands-handbags-scarcity-resale), this triggers a perception of scarcity, which then leads to boosted prices and, in turn, surging demand. How have FASHIONPHILE shoppers responded to these increases in real time?

Where there’s a price increase, there’s a boost in sales. FASHIONPHILE sales for Chanel experienced a significant surge in March 2023, increasing by 47% compared to the previous six-month average. Subsequently, sales returned to their usual average levels after, followed by a rise in quotes which rose 43% in March compared to the previous six months and has remained 17% higher than the previous average in the months since March.

Hermès Prices Are Already Up - Happy (Sorta) New Year?!

![Image 3](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/1bea7fbd9a0f8740f02ddbcb9772ea351b09ca5392159fe57aba1a577c1834ec?s=40&d=mm&r=pg)

Jan 5, 2024

Happy 2024 – have you recovered from your New Year’s hangover yet? You might want to bring back the tequila and pick up where you left off.

## Hermès Price Increase in 2024: An Unexpected Start

This year, Hermès decided to dispense with the usual full month of preparation for its annual price increases – which usually start somewhere around the beginning of February and proceed, by metièr, over the course of a few weeks – and hit US clients pretty much while they were still _sleeping it off_.

## Global Impact: Hermès Price Changes Across Continents

While European and Asian clients have not been given that consideration and are used to new prices hitting the market pretty much as soon as the ball drops (and some countries, such as China, saw some price increases as early as December 22), Americans, and now most of the world, has been brought into line time-wise, _if not price-wise_, with all increases happening within roughly the same period.

![Image 4: hermes herbag zip cabine bag](https://www.purseblog.com/images/2024/01/hermes-herbag-zip-cabine-bag-600x600.webp)

The Hermès Zip Carabine Bag leads the US bag price hike with a 10.20% increase year-over-year.

It now retails for $5,400, up from $4,900 in 2023.

These are still implemented by department and are rolled out over two or three weeks, but they have certainly begun in earnest. Already, we have seen price changes in leather goods (January 2) and shoes (January 3), with ready-to-wear increases expected today.

## Reasons Behind the Hermès Price Hike

Europe saw their increases begin to be implemented last week, and clients everywhere note the higher prices. Why the price hikes?

Hermès, like many companies, cites added costs for raw materials and labor, which is not unusual, although increased inflation has affected markets everywhere.

Of course, at this point, the client has come to expect price increases; over the past twenty years or so, the entire luxury fashion industry has shifted (a point which I previously lamented in my [Price Increase article](http://purseblog.com/hermes/update-on-hermes-bag-prices-february-2022/) from 2022) from making price changes a rare occurrence to a regular event.

In turn, it wouldn’t be a surprise to understand that brands have come to expect these regular increases and rely on them to whatever extent in anticipation of future profits.

## Pre-Increase Purchasing: A Strategy to Avoid Higher Prices

The bump in income comes not only from the increased price; the effects of a price change begin before the new prices take effect.

This is due to the anticipation of an upcoming price change, which stirs clients to buy whatever they have been considering for fear that they will have to pay more for the same item if they wait too long.

## Analyzing the Extent of Price Increases on Hermès Products

Although the big numbers get everyone’s attention, the amount of the increase varies per item. For shoes, prices have gone up more than 10%, with Orans going from $700 to $760, Paris Loafers from $1,100 to $1,225, Bouncing Sneakers from $920 to $990, and Chypre Sandals from $780 to $910.

It appears that leather goods have increased from about 3% to about 15%, with many increases hovering in the usual 6-7% range.

**China** saw bags go up at an average of around 10%, with some bags increasing by as much as 20%.

Clients in **Singapore** are reporting increases of about 10%.
